pr_body:
When running under Rack 3, we'll proceed with the new behaviour. That means we won't affect applications that already use Rack 3, but does also mean we can't help an application that is simultaneously bumping Rails and Rack together. 🤷🏻‍♂️

However, with this commit, we at least ensure we maintain compatibility for applications that are currently still on Rack 2 -- and we can help with the transition using deprecation warnings... though there's admittedly a decent chance such warnings will only show up in production.

Fixes #53394
pr_comments:
> though there's admittedly a decent chance such warnings will only show up in production.

That's good to know; at least folks looking to upgrade Rack 3 can use those logs to update their setup.

This change applies **also to request body params** passed as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, not just query params. I haven't dug deeply, but it is probably a consequence of https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53193 paired with this change. Is this behavior expected?

Example:

```ruby
require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  # with Rack 2 param parsing backward compat
  gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main", ref: "ae60fcebafaa102df50504425e8113e3648c5faa"

  # without Rack 2 compat
  # gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main", ref: "902d99c8c579c3e3d286d658d7c718d055e408cf"

  gem "rack", "~> 2"
end

require "minitest/autorun"
require "rack/test"

class BugTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include Rack::Test::Methods

  def test_action_dispatch_parse_query_parameters
    env = {
      "REQUEST_METHOD" => "POST",
      "rack.input" => StringIO.new("content=just-one;param"),
      "CONTENT_LENGTH" => "22",
      "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
    }
    request = ActionDispatch::Request.new(env)
    params = request.query_parameters
    expected = { "content" => "just-one;param" }
    assert_equal(expected, request.params)
  end
end
```

/cc @matthewd
/cc @matthewd in case you lost the notification 😅🙇‍♂️

issue_context.title: Regression in request parameter parsing
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53193 causes a change of behaviour if using Rack 2. This might be considered a bug fix, but it's a non-trivial change so I thought it was worth getting some eyes over.

The issue occurs when requesting a URL that looks like this: `"/foo?date=2024-10-21&user_id=123"`. With Rack 2, before https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53193, this was parsed as:

```
{"date"=>"2024-10-21", "amp"=>nil, "user_id"=>"123", "controller"=>"test", "action"=>"index"}
```

After https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53193 it is parsed as:

```
{"date"=>"2024-10-21", "amp;user_id"=>"123", "controller"=>"test", "action"=>"index"}
```

If you use Rack 3, it parses as the latter form regardless of Rails commit.

So https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53193 causes a change in behaviour for Rack 2 users. Arguably it's a bug fix in Rails, and the user should fix their buggy code (they should go to `"/foo?date=2024-10-21&user_id=123"` instead). But it's a pretty subtle bug that's hard to audit for and that's been around for a very long time.

What makes it particularly subtle is that the "buggy" code results in expected params, ie. if you do `params[:user_id]` in your controller it'll return what you expect. On upgrading to the "fixed" version of Rails, will `params[:user_id]` return `nil` instead of a value.

<!-- (Guidelines for creating a bug report are [available
here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#creating-a-bug-report)) -->

<!-- Paste your executable test case created from one of the scripts found [here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#create-an-executable-test-case) below: -->
```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  # The last commit before https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53193, tests fail.
  gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main", ref: "e83cfa5466255d48cf03308dfe5d183eb8444d51"

  # The commit for https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/53193, tests pass
  # gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main", ref: "d64611bc5a71a749d10c4da295e80fe182b5d7ea"

  # The issue is specific to Rack 2.
  gem "rack", "~> 2"

  # If you use Rack 3 the tests pass with either Rails commit.
  # gem "rack", "~> 3"
end

require "action_controller/railtie"

class TestApp < Rails::Application
  config.root = __dir__
  config.hosts << "example.org"
  config.secret_key_base = "secret_key_base"

  config.logger = Logger.new($stdout)
  Rails.logger  = config.logger

  routes.draw do
    get "/foo" => "test#index"
  end
end

class TestController < ActionController::Base
  include Rails.application.routes.url_helpers

  def index
    render plain: params.to_s
  end
end

require "minitest/autorun"
require "rack/test"

class BugTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include Rack::Test::Methods

  def test_returns_success
    get "/foo?date=2024-10-21&user_id=123"
    expected = %Q({"date"=>"2024-10-21", "amp;user_id"=>"123", "controller"=>"test", "action"=>"index"})
    assert_equal expected, last_response.body

    # before PR 53193, this would pass:
    # expected = %Q({"date"=>"2024-10-21", "amp"=>nil, "user_id"=>"123", "controller"=>"test", "action"=>"index"})
    # assert_equal expected, last_response.body
  end

  private
    def app
      Rails.application
    end
end

```

### Expected behavior

Honestly I'm not sure the right approach here. It would suit me if the old behaviour was supported forever, but objectively that seems silly given that it's clearly a bug.

### Actual behavior

See above

### System configuration
**Rails version**: main

**Ruby version**: 3.3
comments: If this is Rack 2 only, perhaps it can be a motivator for https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/50565?

Thanks for noticing and reporting this!

I picked up Rack 3's fix of https://github.com/rack/rack/issues/1732, which was not intentional... though the alternatives of allowing both characters for everyone, or conditioning our behaviour on the Rack version, both seem also-not-great.

🤔

@matthewd would you consider a Rails config and/or deprecation for this? The consensus on that Rack issue was that this could be a big breaking change (confirmed!), so I think that would ease the upgrade path now that we are decoupling from Rack a bit more. If you're 👍 on this, I can work on it.

Yeah, my current thought is that the best option might be to silently adopt the Rack 3 behaviour if Rack 3 (or more accurately, not-Rack-2) is present [so we don't regress/change behaviour for people already using Rack 3], but then when Rack 2, use a config setting:

Default to `"&;"`, `load_defaults` it to `"&"`, deprecation warning if the application doesn't set it (and is using Rack 2).

If the config is set, we should follow it regardless of Rack version.

That way: if someone is already on Rack 3 [or upgrades to Rack 3 at the same time as Rails 8.0], they have already [or will then] follow the Rack 3 upgrade path (silent switch-over, 🤷🏻‍♂️)... but anyone who upgrades to Rails 8.0 while still on Rack 2 will keep the Rack 2 behaviour for now, while we can also proactively nudge them to be explicit about what they want.

(All the "middleware/proxies might disagree = danger zone" stuff applies as soon as Rails and Rack apply different opinions, as we would via this config, but I think informed danger is probably a more workable upgrade path than safe breakage.)

Hey folks, wanted to add another example of a regression that appeared after upgrading Rails to include parsing changes.

In our case the application started to parse queries with nested structure in a different (broken) way. However while preparing the reproduction script I realized that in our case the same failure happens when using rack `3` which I suppose means that the application is the one that needs to change here as it won't be compatible with rack 3. And the change in Rails just revealed this incompatibility earlier. 

So I'm mainly sharing for additional and to potentially think of a possibility to provide a better heads-up for applications that may experience the same.

On a side note, I'd like to learn if `[cart][apple]=1&[cart][banana]=2"` format was even officially supported or just happened to work. Because if it was intentionally supported it could mean much higher rate of applications relying on it and breaking in ambiguous ways when migrating to rack3 or next rails version.
**Update**:  https://github.com/rack/rack/issues/2128 this leads me to believe that it should be considered an application problem 

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script</summary>

  ```ruby
  require "bundler/inline"

  gemfile(true) do
    source "https://rubygems.org"

    # with parsing changes
    gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main", ref: "d64611bc5a71a749d10c4da295e80fe182b5d7ea"

    # without parsing changes
    # gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main", ref: "e83cfa5466255d48cf03308dfe5d183eb8444d51"

    gem "rack", "~> 2"
  end

  require "action_controller/railtie"

  class TestApp < Rails::Application
    config.root = __dir__
    config.hosts << "example.org"
    config.secret_key_base = "secret_key_base"

    config.logger = Logger.new($stdout)
    Rails.logger  = config.logger

    routes.draw do
      get "/foo" => "test#index"
    end
  end

  class TestController < ActionController::Base
    include Rails.application.routes.url_helpers

    def index
      render(plain: params.to_s)
    end
  end

  require "minitest/autorun"
  require "rack/test"

  class BugTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
    include Rack::Test::Methods

    QUERIES = [
      "cart[apple]=1&cart[banana]=2", # the only format that keeps working against any version rails/rack
      "[cart][apple]=1&[cart][banana]=2",
      "cart%5D%5Bapple%5D=1&%5Bcart%5D%5Bbanana%5D=2",
    ]

    def test_controller_returns_success
      expected = %({"cart"=>{"apple"=>"1", "banana"=>"2"}, "controller"=>"test", "action"=>"index"})
      QUERIES.each_with_index do |query, index|
        get("/foo?#{query}")
        assert_equal(expected, last_response.body, "Query with index #{index} failed. Query: #{query}")
      end
    end

    def test_action_dispatch_parse_query_parameters
      QUERIES.each_with_index do |query, index|
        env = {
          "QUERY_STRING" => query,
          "REQUEST_METHOD" => "GET",
          "rack.input" => StringIO.new,
          "CONTENT_LENGTH" => "0",
          "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
        }
        request = ActionDispatch::Request.new(env)
        params = request.query_parameters
        expected = { "cart" => { "apple" => "1", "banana" => "2" } }
        assert_equal(expected, params, "Query with index #{index} failed. Query: #{query}")
      end
    end

    private

    def app
      Rails.application
    end
  end
  ```

</details>

review_comments: Should these configs be documented? My understanding is that you should use them if you're upgrading from Rack 2 to Rack 3 but want to preserve Rack 2 behaviour for a little while longer. And also that they will both be removed in Rails 8.1?
